title: A weekly meeting for the API

blocks.text: A weekly meeting is set up in its organiser's zone, and the public API sends each occurrence as an `OffsetDateTime`, which carries a plain UTC offset and no zone rules.

Write `Recurring.occurrences(ZonedDateTime first, int count)`: the first `count` occurrences, one week apart, starting with `first` itself, offset included. The meeting keeps its wall-clock time in its zone, so **the offset changes** when daylight saving starts or ends. Occurrence `k` is `k` weeks after `first`; when that week's time does not exist, because the clocks skip it, the meeting is held at the time the zone moves it to, and the weeks after are not affected.

cases.says: Three winter weeks give 09:00 at -05:00 each week.
A 09:00 meeting stays at 09:00 across both DST changes; its offset moves between -05:00 and -04:00.
A 02:30 meeting falls at 03:30 on the spring-forward day and is back at 02:30 the week after.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A ZonedDateTime carries its zone's rules, so its offset changes with daylight saving, while an OffsetDateTime keeps one fixed offset.
